report.source_text: Histopathologic examination revealed a dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate throughout the entire superficial dermis. The epidermis presented thickening and elongation of the rete ridges – which correspond to the clinical features of the disease – along with the presence of eosionophilic bodies and exocytosis of lymphocytes (Figure 2). We observed no signs of neoplasia or malignancy.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with a lobulated warty lesion on the lower lip that first appeared during her first pregnancy approximately 7 years ago and spontaneously regressed. The lesion recurred during her second pregnancy approximately 5 years ago and has progressively worsened since then. Initial dental examination prompted biopsy. Histopathology revealed a dense predominantly plasmocytic infiltrate throughout the superficial dermis with epidermal thickening, rete ridge elongation, eosinophilic bodies, and lymphocytic exocytosis, with no signs of neoplasia or malignancy. Immunohistochemical staining confirmed polyclonal plasma cell infiltration (CD138+, kappa+, lambda+), establishing the diagnosis of plasmoacanthoma. The patient was treated with three consecutive monthly intralesional injections of triamcinolone acetonide (20 mg/ml, 1 ml per dose), resulting in gradual improvement with no recurrence documented over the subsequent 6 months.
